_meta.description: What authored text the v2 renderer needs. The words themselves live in the shared callout registry under module 'tabs' and are edited in the Callout Editor; this file is the renderer's contract with them. Validated at build time by report_text.R — a key here with no entry in the registry, or a placeholder in the registry that is not declared here, refuses the build.
_meta.format: key -> { page, context, tokens }. page groups the entry in the Callout Editor and should match a v2 tab. context says where on that tab it renders, so an author knows what they are changing. tokens lists the {placeholders} the renderer supplies for that key; any other {lower_snake_case} in the authored text is a typo and refuses the build.
_meta.authoring:
Text is the CONTENT of its block — the renderer supplies the surrounding

/

and the data-txt-key tag. Inline markup is limited to strong em b i br p ul ol li h3 h4 span code sup sub, balanced, with no attributes. Blank text renders nothing at all, which is how an author switches a block off without touching code.

report.construction.produced.context: About card, Report construction — the attribution sentence. Always rendered, and prepended to a study's own _REPORT_CONSTRUCTION note unless that note names the producer itself.

report.construction.computed.context: About card, Report construction — completes the attribution paragraph. Stock note only; a study's own _REPORT_CONSTRUCTION replaces it.

report.construction.self_contained.context: About card, Report construction — what the file is and what recalculates as the reader clicks. Stock note only.

report.construction.prior_waves_publishe.context: About card, Report construction — rendered ONLY when the report carries earlier waves and none of them holds respondent-level scores, i.e. when the figures really are carried forward rather than recalculated. Stock note only.

report.construction.ai_and_review.context: About card, Report construction — where AI does and does not act, and who is accountable. Stock note only; a study's own _REPORT_CONSTRUCTION replaces this too, and then owns the disclosure.

reader.legend.sig_letters.context: Legend panel, Significance letters — what a lettered cell means and what case signifies.

reader.legend.low_base.context: Legend panel, Significance letters — only when the project sets a low-base threshold.

reader.legend.arrows_profile.context: Legend panel, Arrows & change chips — arrows on a composite (profile) column.

reader.legend.arrows_chips.context: Legend panel, Arrows & change chips — wave-on-wave change chips.

reader.legend.bands.context: Legend panel, Score bands — {bands} is the study's own banding, read off its questions.

reader.legend.row_kinds.context: Legend panel, Score bands — what NET and Index rows are.

reader.legend.moe_with_base.context: Legend panel, margin of error — when a published total base is known, so real numbers can be quoted.

reader.legend.moe_no_base.context: Legend panel, margin of error — the same point when no base is available to quote.

reader.legend.weighted_fallback.context: Legend panel, Weighted data — only when the filter bar has no fuller weighting note to show.

reader.legend.explain_toggle.context: Legend panel, Explain significance — the label beside the plain-language toggle.

cards.reading.heatmap.context: 'Reading this table' — what cell shading means.

cards.reading.published_computed.context: 'Reading this table' — the PUBLISHED / COMPUTED distinction. The one thing a reader must understand about a live report.

cards.reading.row_kinds.context: 'Reading this table' — NET and Index rows, sorting, hiding, the wave strip.

cards.reading.see_legend.context: 'Reading this table' — points at the How-to-read panel. {legend_link} is the button the renderer supplies.

cards.reading.insight_box.context: 'Reading this table' — what the analyst's Insight box does and where its note is kept.

cards.sig.what_it_answers.context: 'Understanding the significance testing' — what the test answers and why sample size decides it.

cards.sig.which_test.context: 'Understanding the significance testing' — z-test for percentages, Welch for means.

cards.sig.letters.context: 'Understanding the significance testing' — how to read the letters. {min_base} is the project's low-base threshold, so a study on a different threshold is described correctly.

cards.sig.multiplicity.context: 'Understanding the significance testing' — why many comparisons need a correction, and which one Turas uses.

cards.sig.wave_exception.context: 'Understanding the significance testing' — why wave-on-wave comparisons take no correction.

cards.sig.real_vs_important.context: 'Understanding the significance testing' — significance is not importance.

conf.footer.example.context: Precision footer — the worked example, in the report's own numbers. {range_meaning} is one of the two keys below.

conf.footer.range_meaning_group.context: Precision footer — how the example's range reads when a finite population correction applies (it describes the whole group).

conf.footer.range_meaning_rerun.context: Precision footer — how the example's range reads without a correction (it describes a re-run).

conf.footer.what_95_means.context: Precision footer — what 95% means. Probability samples only.

conf.footer.reading_ranges.context: Precision footer — the honest equivalent for a non-probability design, where 95% is not a coverage guarantee.

conf.footer.small_samples.context: Precision footer — only when the report has a small column worth naming.

conf.footer.comparing.context: Precision footer — overlapping ranges mean the difference is noise.

conf.footer.significant_means.context: Precision footer — what 'significant' does and does not claim.

conf.design.probability.context: Precision footer, About this survey — a probability design.

conf.design.non_probability.context: Precision footer, About this survey — a non-probability design; the ranges are stability intervals, not confidence intervals.

conf.design.cluster.context: Precision footer, About this survey — a cluster sample, whose clustering Turas does not adjust for.

conf.fpc.lead_census_rate.context: Precision footer, finite population correction — opening clause for a declared census where the response rate is known.

conf.fpc.lead_sample_rate.context: Precision footer, finite population correction — opening clause for a sample whose coverage of the universe is known.

conf.fpc.lead_known_sizes.context: Precision footer, finite population correction — opening clause when group sizes are known but no response rate is.

conf.fpc.body_census.context: Precision footer, finite population correction — the census case, where non-response is the uncertainty that remains.

conf.fpc.body_sample.context: Precision footer, finite population correction — the sample case, where sampling uncertainty is unchanged because most of the universe was never asked.

tracking.unmatched.lead.context: Tracking summary — shown when prior waves loaded but nothing matched. {priors} is the count, {span} the wave range.

tracking.unmatched.cause.context: Tracking summary — the usual cause, and the config setting that fixes it.

tracking.heatmap.legend.context: Tracking summary — the heatmap's reading note. {soft_clause} appears only when the 80% level is switched on.

tracking.heatmap.soft_clause.context: Tracking summary — the hollow-arrow clause spliced into the heatmap note when the 80% level is on.

tracking.scorecard.bands.context: Tracking summary — how the key-metric cards are coloured.

tracking.pulse.not_testable_tip.context: Tracking summary — tooltip on the 'not testable' pulse chip.

tracking.pulse.sigmode_tip.context: Tracking summary — tooltip on the significance-level selector.

tracking.changes.none.context: Tracking summary — no significant wave-on-wave changes, and the history could support a test.

tracking.changes.untestable.context: Tracking summary — no test could run at all because the historical bases were not loaded.

tracking.soft.intro.context: Tracking summary — the 'nearly significant' card block.

tracking.method.how_tested.context: Tracking summary — the collapsed 'How wave-on-wave changes are tested' note.

tracking.empty.context: Tracking tab — shown when no wave history is configured at all.

visualise.legend.significance.context: Tracking visualise — what a coloured arrow means and which test produced it.

visualise.ci_tip.context: Tracking visualise — tooltip on the interval-bands toggle.

visualise.trendline_tip.context: Tracking visualise — tooltip on the trendline toggle.

visualise.ci_note.context: Tracking visualise — the note under the chart when interval bands are on. {softened} is added for non-probability designs.

visualise.ci_note_softened.context: Tracking visualise — the clause added to the interval note when the design is not a formal random sample.

visualise.note_tags.context: Tracking visualise — how to tag a data point with a note.
